content.text: {"primary_meaning": "In Christian teaching, scarlet most commonly symbolizes sin — deep-dyed, conspicuous guilt — with the closely paired idea that such sin can be cleansed and made 'white as snow.' The color's fastness as a dye (kermes/tola'at shani) is often cited to explain why it images sin's ingrained, seemingly permanent stain.", "primary_basis": ["Isaiah 1:18 ('though your sins be as scarlet, they shall be as white as snow; though they be red like crimson, they shall be as wool')", "Revelation 17:3-4 (the woman arrayed in purple and scarlet, associated with abomination and immorality)", "Revelation 18:16 (Babylon clothed in scarlet as emblem of corrupt luxury)"], "alternatives": [{"meaning": "Blood, sacrifice, and atonement — scarlet as a pointer to sacrificial blood and, typologically, to the blood of Christ (e.g., the scarlet cord of Rahab read as a type of salvation through Christ's blood; scarlet wool in purification rites).", "basis": ["Joshua 2:18, 21 (Rahab's scarlet cord)", "Leviticus 14:4-6, 49-52 (scarlet in cleansing rituals)", "Numbers 19:6 (scarlet in the red heifer rite)", "Hebrews 9:19 (scarlet wool used in sprinkling blood of the covenant)"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "Royalty, wealth, luxury, and worldly splendor — scarlet as a costly dye worn by the rich and powerful, sometimes with an ironic or judgmental edge.", "basis": ["2 Samuel 1:24 (Saul clothed daughters of Israel in scarlet)", "Proverbs 31:21 (household clothed in scarlet)", "Matthew 27:28 (soldiers put a scarlet robe on Jesus in mock royalty)", "Lamentations 4:5 (those brought up in scarlet)", "Revelation 18:12, 16 (merchandise and clothing of Babylon)"], "prominence": "common"}, {"meaning": "In tabernacle typology, scarlet (with blue and purple in the curtains and priestly garments) is read devotionally as pointing to Christ's humanity, suffering, or sacrificial death.", "basis": ["Exodus 25:4; 26:1, 31, 36; 28:5-6 (scarlet yarn in the tabernacle and priestly vestments)"], "prominence": "minority"}, {"meaning": "Scarlet as a mark of harlotry, apostasy, or the corrupt world system specifically (the 'scarlet woman' of Revelation as an emblem of false religion or Babylon), sometimes treated as a distinct symbol rather than a subset of sin generally.", "basis": ["Revelation 17:1-6 (the great harlot in scarlet, the scarlet beast)"], "prominence": "common"}], "has_settled_consensus": true, "confidence": "high", "notes": "Scarlet is a polyvalent color symbol in Scripture, but Isaiah 1:18 has made 'sin (and its cleansing)' the dominant reflexive association in sermons, hymns, and popular teaching. The blood/atonement reading (especially Rahab's cord as a type of Christ's blood, a reading going back to patristic writers such as Clement of Rome, 1 Clement 12) and the luxury/royalty reading are both well established and not mutually exclusive with the primary meaning; many interpreters treat scarlet's meaning as context-dependent rather than fixed. Tabernacle color typology is popular in some devotional and dispensational circles but is not mainstream academic exegesis."}
